question: A team is designing the system prompt for a support agent and wants Claude to reliably distinguish between cases that should be escalated and cases it can resolve autonomously. Which approach best achieves this?
options: A) Add explicit escalation criteria plus few-shot examples showing both escalation and resolution cases
B) Rely on the agent's general training to infer appropriate escalation behavior without adding specific guidance
C) Instruct the agent to escalate whenever its own self-reported confidence falls below a fixed threshold
D) Instruct the agent to escalate whenever the customer's message contains any negative language or urgency
correct_answers: A) Add explicit escalation criteria plus few-shot examples showing both escalation and resolution cases
explanations: Correct - explicit, example-driven criteria give the agent concrete patterns to distinguish escalation-worthy cases from ones it can resolve directly.
Incorrect - relying on general training without explicit, scenario-specific guidance leaves escalation behavior inconsistent and unpredictable.
Incorrect - self-reported confidence thresholds are an unreliable proxy for real case complexity and shouldn't drive escalation decisions.
Incorrect - negative language or urgency reflects sentiment, which is an unreliable proxy for whether a case actually needs escalation.
